title: Dasaratha's grief and anguish
introduction: In this chapter, Sage Valmiki describes the bitter agony of Dasaratha on hearing to the adamant Kaikeyi's words.
closing: || इत्यार्शे स्रीमद्रामायने आदिकाव्ये अयोध्यकान्दे त्रयोदशः सर्गः ||

verses.devanagari:
अतदर्हं महाराजं शयानम् सयानमतथोचितम् |
ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकात्परिच्युतम्
अनर्थरूपा सिद्धार्था ह्यभीता भयदर्शिनी |
पुनराकारयामास तमेव वरमङ्गना
verses.iast:
atat arham mahā rājam śayānam atathā ucitam |
yayātim iva puṇya ante deva lokāt paricyutam
anartha rūpā siddha arthāabhītā bhaya darśinī |
punar ākārayām āsa tam eva varam anganā
verses.translation: Dasaratha was not suitable for such an unfortunate condition nor was he habituated to such a situation. He was lying down on the floor, as king Yayati who fell down on earth fter exhausting his merit in the region of heaven. Kaikeyi who was a manifestation of worthlessness who accomplished her desire, who was fearlessly exhibiting her fearful form, asked for those boons again in a loud voice, to Dasaratha who was in such a bad mood situation.

glosses.meaning: who was a manifesting of worthlessness
who was not habitated to such a situation
who was lying down on floor

verses.devanagari:
त्वं कत्थसे महाराज सत्यवादी दृढव्रतः |
मम चेदं वरं कस्माद्विधारयितुमिच्छसि
verses.iast:
tvam katthase mahā rāja satya vādī dRḍha vrataḥ |
mama ca imam varam kasmāt vidhārayitum iccasi
verses.translation: "Oh, king! You always boast yourself, saying "I speak truth. I am persisted in my promise." Now, why are you objecting to my boon?"

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु कैकेय्या राजा दशरथस्तदा |
प्रत्युवाच ततः क्रुद्धो मुहूर्तं विह्वलन्निव
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu kaikeyyā rājā daśa rathaḥ tadā |
pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtam vihvalann iva
verses.translation: After thus spoken to by Kaikeyi, Dasaratha became angry, turned out delirious for a moment and again spoke as follows:

verses.devanagari:
मृते मयि गते रामे वनं मनुजपुंगवे |
हन्त अनार्ये मम अमित्रे सकाम सुखिनी भव
verses.iast:
mRte mayi gate rāme vanam manuja pumgave |
hanta anārye mama amitre rāmaḥ pravrājitaḥ vanam
verses.translation: "Oh, the vulgar one! You, my enemy! You want to be happy after your desire is fulfilled when Rama the best among men leaves for the forest and when I die thereafter. Alas!"

glosses.meaning: when Rama the best among men leaves for forest

verses.devanagari:
स्वर्गेऽपि खलु रामस्य कुशलं दैवतैरहम् |
प्रत्यादेशादभिहितं धारयिष्ये कथं बत
verses.iast:
svarge'pi khalu rāmasya kuśalaṃ daivatairahm |
pratyādeśādabhihitaṃ dhārayiśhye kathaṃ bata
verses.translation: "When celestials ask for me about Rama's well-being after I reach heaven, how can I indeed convince them that he is well obscuringly the actual fact?"

verses.devanagari:
कैकेय्याः प्रियकामेन रामः प्रव्राजितो मया |
यदि सत्यं ब्रवीम्येतत्तस्त्यं भविष्यति
verses.iast:
kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmena rāmaḥ pravrājito mayā |
yadi satyam bravīmy etat tat asatyam bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "If I tell without obscuring the fact that I sent Rama to exile desirous of showing kindness to Kaikeyi, nobody will believe me."

verses.devanagari:
अपुत्रेण मया पुत्रः श्रमेण महता महान् |
रामो लब्धो महाबाहुः स कथं त्यज्यते मया
verses.iast:
aputreṇa mayā putraḥ śrameṇa mahatā mahān |
rāmo labdho mahābāhuḥ sa kathaṃ tyajyate mayā
verses.translation: "With much effort I, the childless begot the great and powerful Rama as my son. How can I abandon such Rama?"

verses.devanagari:
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च जितक्रोधः क्षमापरः |
कथं कमलपत्राक्षो मया रामो विवास्यते
verses.iast:
śūrśca kṛtavidyaśca jitakrodhaḥ kśamāparaḥ |
kathaṃ kamalapatrākśo mayā rāmo vivāsyate
verses.translation: "How can I send away Rama who is valiant and knowledgeable, who has subdued anger, who has forbearance and who has eyes like lotus-petals".

glosses.meaning: who is solely devoted to patience
who has eyes like lotus petals

verses.devanagari:
कथमिन्दीवरश्यामं दीर्घबाहुं महाबलम् |
अभिराममहं रामं प्रेषयिष्यामि दण्डकान्
verses.iast:
kathamindīvaraśyāmaṃ dīrghabāhuṃ mahābalam |
abhirāmamahaṃ rāmam preśhayiśhyāmi daṇḍakān
verses.translation: "How I can I send Rama, who is dark blue in colour like a blue lotus, who is long-armed , who is very strong and graceful, to Dandaka forest?"

glosses.meaning: who is dark blue in colour like a blue lotus

verses.devanagari:
सुखानामुचितस्यैव दुःखैरनुचितस्य च |
दुःखं नामानुपश्येयं कथं रामस्य धीमतः
verses.iast:
sukhānāmucitasyaiva duḥkhairanucitasya ca |
duḥkhaṃ nāmānupaśyeyaṃ kathaṃ rāmasya dhīmataḥ
verses.translation: "Rama is accustomed to comforts. He is not accustomed to difficulties. How can I imagine such sensible Rama in a troublesome situation?"

verses.devanagari:
यदि दुःखमकृत्वाद्य मम संक्रमणं भवेत् |
अदुःखार्हस्य रामस्य ततः सुखमवाप्नुयाम्
verses.iast:
yadi duḥkhamakṛtvādya mama saṅkramaṇaṃ bhavet |
aduḥkhārhasya rāmasya tataḥ sukhamavāpnu yām

verses.devanagari:
नृशंसे पापसंकल्पे रामं स्त्यपराक्रमम् |
किं विप्रियेण कैकेयि प्रियं योजयसे मम
अकीर्तिरतुला लोके ध्रुवः परिभवश्च मे |
verses.iast:
nṛśaṃse pāpasaṅkalpe rāmaṃ styaparākramam |
kim vipriyeṇa kaikeyi priyaṃ yojayase mama
akīrtiratulā loke dhruvaḥ paribhavaśca me |
verses.translation: "Oh, cruel one! One with sinful thoughts! Oh, kaikeyi! why are you planning to do harm to Rama who is beloved to me and who is truly heroic? I shall certainly get unequalled ill fame and humiliation in this world".

glosses.meaning: one with sinful thoughts! kaikeyii = Oh
who is truly heroic ? atulaa = uneaqualled

verses.devanagari:
तथा विलपतस्तस्य परिभ्रमित चेतसः
अस्तमभ्यगमत्सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत |
verses.iast:
tathā vilapataḥ tasya paribhramita cetasaḥ
astam abhyagamat sūryo rajanī ca abhyavartata |
verses.translation: While Dasaratha was thus lamenting with his disturbed mind, there was approach of night with setting of the sun.

verses.devanagari:
सा त्रियामा तथार्तस्य चन्द्रमण्डलमण्डिता
राज्ञो विलपमानस्य न व्यभासत शर्वरी |
verses.iast:
sā tri yāmā tathā ārtasya candra maṇḍala maṇḍitā
rāGYo vilapamānasya na vyabhāsata śarvarī |
verses.translation: To Dasaratha, who was thus lamenting painfully, the night seemed to be dark even though it was adorned with charming circular moon.

glosses.meaning: eventhough it was adorned with circular moon.

verses.devanagari:
तथैवोष्णम् विनिःश्वस्य वृद्धो दसरथो नृपः
विललापार्तवद्दुःखं गगनासक्तलोचनः |
verses.iast:
tathaiva uṣṇam vinihśvasya vRddho daśaratho nRpaḥ
vilalāpa ārtavad duhkham gagana āsakta locanaḥ |
verses.translation: The aged Dasaratha was lamenting painfully as though afflicted with a disease, with lot and hard breaths, having his eyes fixed on the sky.

glosses.meaning: having his eyes fixed on sky.

verses.devanagari:
प्रभातं त्वयेच्छामि निशे नक्षत्रभूषणे
क्रियतां मे दया भद्रे मयायं रचितोऽञ्जलिः |
verses.iast:
na prabhātam tvayā iccāmi mayā ayam racitaḥ anjaliḥ
athavā gamyatām śīghram na aham iccāmi nirghRṇām |
verses.translation: "Oh, auspicious night, decorated with stars! do not wish you to do break into a dawn. Have mercy on me. I pray with folded hands."

glosses.meaning: decorated with stars! na ichchaami = I do not wish

verses.devanagari:
अथवा गम्यतां शीघ्रं नाहमिच्छामि निर्घृणाम्
नृशंसां कैकेयीं द्रष्टुं यत्कृते व्यसनं महत् |
verses.iast:
atha vā gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ nāhamicchāmi nirghṛṇām
nRśaṃsām kaikeyīm draṣṭum yat kRte vyasanam mahat |
verses.translation: "Otherwise, Oh, Night! Leave away quickly. I do not went to see Kaikeyi, who is shameless, cruel and for whose reason this great calamity occurred"

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा कैकेयीं संयताञ्जलिः
प्रसादयामास पुनः कैकेयीं चेदमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
evam uktvā tataḥ rājā kaikeyīm samyata anjaliḥ
prasādayām āsa punaḥ kaikeyīm ca idam abravīt |
verses.translation: The king spoke like this and beseeched kaikeyi with folded hands. He again spoke this word to Kaikeyi.

verses.devanagari:
साधुवृत्तस्य दीनस्य त्वद्गतस्य गतायुषः |
प्रसादः क्रियतां देवि भद्रे राज्ञो विशेषतः |
verses.iast:
sādhu vRttasya dīnasya tvad gatasya gata āyuṣaḥ |
prasādaḥ kriyatām devi bhadre rāGYo viśeṣataḥ |
verses.translation: "Oh, auspicious queen! I am a well conducted man. I am dejected and seeking refuse in you. I am an old man and especially a king. Be kind to me."

glosses.meaning: one who sought refuse in you

verses.devanagari:
शून्ये न खलु सुश्रोणि मयेदं समुदाहृतम्
कुरु साधु प्रसादं मे बाले सहृदया ह्यसि |
verses.iast:
śūnyena khalu suśroṇi mayā idam samudāhRtam
kuru sādhu prasādam me bāle sahRdayā hi asi |
verses.translation: "Oh, well-hipped one! I hope that whatever I told, has not merged in the sky. Oh! young woman, be kind to me . You are good-hearted."

verses.devanagari:
प्रसीद देवि रामो मे त्वद्धत्तं राज्यमव्ययम्
लभतामसितापाङ्गे यशः परमवाप्नुहि |
verses.iast:
prasīda devi rāmo me tvaddhattaṃ rājyamavyayam
labhatāmasitāpāṇ^ge yaśaḥ paramavāpnuhi |
verses.translation: "Oh, queen with dark outer corner of eyes be kind. You your self give my kingdom to Rama. Thus, you will obtain great fame."

glosses.meaning: with dark outer corner of eyes

verses.devanagari:
मम रामस्य लोकस्य गुरूणां भरतस्य च
प्रियमेतद्गुरुश्रोणि कुरु चारुमुखेक्षणे |
verses.iast:
mama rāmasya lokasya gurūṇāṃ bharatasya ca
priyametadguruśroṇi kuru cārumukhekśaṇe |
verses.translation: "Oh, broad hipped, with beautiful face and eyes! do this. It will be pleasing to me, to Rama, to the world, to priests and to Bharata."

glosses.meaning: to priests bharatasyacha = and to Bharata.

verses.devanagari:
विशुद्धभावस्य सु ुष्टभावा |
दीनस्य ताम्राश्रुकलस्य राज्ञः |
श्रुत्वा विचित्रं करुणं विलापं |
भर्तुर्नृशंसा न चकार वाक्यम्
verses.iast:
viśuddha bhāvasya su duṣṭa bhāvā |
dīnasya tāmrāśrukalasya rājJṇḥ |
śrutvā vicitram karuṇam vilāpam |
bhartur nRśaṃsā na cakāra vākyam
verses.translation: Hearing the king, who was her pure-hearted husband and who was pitifully lamenting strangely with red eyes filled with tears, that bad tempered cruel woman did not follow his words.

glosses.meaning: with red eyes filled with tears

verses.devanagari:
ततः स राजा पुनरेव मूर्छितः |
प्रियामतुष्टां प्रतिकूलभाषिणीम् |
समीक्ष्य पुत्रस्य विवासनम् प्रति |
क्षितौ विसंज्ञो निपपात दुःखितः
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa rājā punar eva mūrcitaḥ |
priyām atuṣṭām pratikūla bhāṣiṇīm |
samīkṣya putrasya vivāsanam prati |
kṣitau visamGYo nipapāta duhkhitaḥ
verses.translation: Seeing his discontented wife talking unpleasantly about sending Rama to forest, that king was distressed, fainted again and fell down unconscious on the floor.

glosses.meaning: about sending the son to forest

verses.devanagari:
इतीव राज्ञो व्यथितस्य सा निशा |
जगाम घोरं श्वसतो मनस्विनः |
विबोध्यमानः प्रतिबोधनं तदा |
निवारयामास स राजसत्तमः
verses.iast:
itīva rājJṇo vythitasya sā niśā |
jagāma ghoraṃ svasato manasvinaḥ |
vibodhyamānaḥ pratibodhanaṃ tadā |
nivārayāmāsa sa rājasattamaḥ
verses.translation: While the distressed and self-respected king was sighing terribly in the way, that night came to an end. In the dawn, bards and singers started to awaken him. But the excellent king prevented them to do.
